title: Lifting a factorization modulo pi^8 (Popescu)
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra and $\pi\in R$ with $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$ and $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)$ (annihilators of $\pi,\pi^2$ in $R$ and of their images in $\Lambda$). Let $A\to\Lambda$ be a homomorphism of $R$-algebras with $A$ of finite presentation over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and assume the image of $\pi$ in $A$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]. Let $A/\pi^8A\to\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ be a factorization, by homomorphisms of $R/\pi^8R$-algebras, of the map $A/\pi^8A\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ induced by $A\to\Lambda$, with $\bar C$ of finite presentation over $R/\pi^8R$. Then there is a factorization $A\to B\to\Lambda$ of $A\to\Lambda$ by homomorphisms of $R$-algebras with $B$ of finite presentation over $R$ such that (a) $R_\pi\to B_\pi$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], where $R_\pi$, $B_\pi$ are the localizations at the powers of $\pi$ (resp. of its image in $B$); (b) the ideal of $\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ generated by the image of $H_{\bar C/(R/\pi^8R)}$ under $\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ is contained in the image in $\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ of $\sqrt{H_{B/R}\Lambda}$, the radical of the ideal of $\Lambda$ generated by the image of $H_{B/R}$ under $B\to\Lambda$; here $H_{\bar C/(R/\pi^8R)}$ and $H_{B/R}$ are singular ideals [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F0 (lemma-desingularize-lifting-apply, line 1862), Section 07CN (section-lifting-lemma); its proof applies Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting) and Lemma 07CT (lemma-desingularize-strictly-standard) and omits the final verification

proof.text: (Annihilators of $\pi^4$.) In any ring $T$ with an element $t$ such that $\mathrm{Ann}_T(t)=\mathrm{Ann}_T(t^2)$ one has $\mathrm{Ann}_T(t^n)=\mathrm{Ann}_T(t)$ for all $n\ge1$: by induction on $n$, if $t^{n+1}x=0$ with $n\ge1$ then $t^2\cdot(t^{n-1}x)=0$, so $t\cdot(t^{n-1}x)=0$, i.e. $t^nx=0$, so $x\in\mathrm{Ann}_T(t^n)=\mathrm{Ann}_T(t)$; the inclusion $\mathrm{Ann}_T(t)\subset\mathrm{Ann}_T(t^n)$ is clear. Applied to $T=R$, $t=\pi$ and to $T=\Lambda$, $t$ the image of $\pi$: $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^4)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^8)=\mathrm{Ann}_R((\pi^4)^2)$ and likewise $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^4)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda((\pi^4)^2)$. So the element $\pi':=\pi^4\in R$ satisfies the annihilator hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lifting], and $\pi'^2=\pi^8$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F0 (lemma-desingularize-lifting-apply, lines 1883-1893)

proof.text: (Apply Lemma 07CP with $\pi^4$ in place of $\pi$.) The structure map $R/\pi^8R\to\bar C$ and the given map $\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras (homomorphisms of $R/\pi^8R$-algebras are $R$-linear), and $\bar C$ is of finite presentation over $R/\pi^8R=R/\pi'^2R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and by Step 1 $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi')=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi'^2)$, $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi')=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi'^2)$. So [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lifting] (Stacks 07CP) applied to $R$, $\Lambda$, $\pi'=\pi^4$ and $R/\pi^8R\to\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ gives an $R$-algebra $D$, a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\delta:D\to\Lambda$ and a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\rho:\bar C\to D/\pi^4D$ such that (i) the composite $\bar C\xrightarrow{\rho}D/\pi^4D\to\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$ ($\delta$ modulo $\pi^4$) equals $\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda\to\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$ (the right square of the diagram), and with (a') $D$ of finite presentation over $R$; (b') $R\to D$ smooth at every prime $\mathfrak q\subset D$ with $\pi^4\notin\mathfrak q$, i.e. with $\pi\notin\mathfrak q$; (c') $R\to D$ smooth at every prime $\mathfrak q\subset D$ with $\pi^4\in\mathfrak q$ such that the prime $\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak q/\pi^4D)$ of $\bar C$ is one at which $R/\pi^8R\to\bar C$ is smooth (smooth at a prime in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F0 (lemma-desingularize-lifting-apply, lines 1883-1893); Lemma Tag 07CP (lemma-lifting, line 1421) with $\pi^4$ for $\pi$

proof.text: (The map $A/\pi^4A\to D/\pi^4D$.) Let $\sigma:A/\pi^8A\to\bar C$ be the first map of the given factorization and $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ the given map. The composite $\psi:A\to A/\pi^8A\xrightarrow{\sigma}\bar C\xrightarrow{\rho}D/\pi^4D$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras; it sends $\pi^4A$ to $\pi^4(D/\pi^4D)=0$, so it factors through an $R$-algebra map $\varphi:A/\pi^4A\to D/\pi^4D$. It is compatible with the maps to $\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$: for $a\in A$, the image of $\varphi(a\bmod\pi^4)=\rho(\sigma(a\bmod\pi^8))$ in $\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$ under $\delta\bmod\pi^4$ equals, by (i) of Step 2, the image of $\sigma(a\bmod\pi^8)$ under $\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda\to\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$, which, as $A/\pi^8A\to\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ factors $\alpha\bmod\pi^8$, is $\alpha(a)\bmod\pi^4\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F0 (lemma-desingularize-lifting-apply, lines 1883-1893)

proof.text: (Apply Lemma 07CT.) The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-desingularize-strictly-standard] (Stacks 07CT) hold for $R$, $\Lambda$, $\pi$, $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ and $\delta:D\to\Lambda$: $R$ is Noetherian; $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$ and $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)$ are hypotheses of the lemma; $A$ is of finite presentation over $R$ by hypothesis and $D$ by (a') of Step 2 [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; (1) the image of $\pi$ in $A$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] by hypothesis; (2) $\varphi$ of Step 3 is an $R$-algebra map $A/\pi^4A\to D/\pi^4D$ compatible with the maps to $\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$. It gives an $R$-algebra $B$ of finite presentation over $R$, a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\beta:B\to\Lambda$ and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $A\to B$, $D\to B$ with $\beta\circ(A\to B)=\alpha$ and $\beta\circ(D\to B)=\delta$, such that $H_{D/R}B\subset H_{B/R}$. In particular $A\to B\to\Lambda$ is a factorization of $\alpha$ by homomorphisms of $R$-algebras with $B$ of finite presentation, as the lemma requires; it remains to prove (a) and (b).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F0 (lemma-desingularize-lifting-apply, lines 1883-1893); Lemma Tag 07CT (lemma-desingularize-strictly-standard, line 1812)

proof.text: ($\pi\in H_{D/R}$, hence the image of $\pi$ lies in $H_{B/R}$.) Let $\mathfrak q\subset D$ be a prime containing $H_{D/R}$. By [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], $V(H_{D/R})$ is the set of primes at which $R\to D$ is not smooth, so $R\to D$ is not smooth at $\mathfrak q$, and by (b') of Step 2, $\pi\in\mathfrak q$. Hence $\pi$ (its image in $D$) lies in $\bigcap_{\mathfrak q\in V(H_{D/R})}\mathfrak q=\sqrt{H_{D/R}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], which is $H_{D/R}$ since $H_{D/R}$ is a radical ideal by definition [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. As $D\to B$ is an $R$-algebra map, the image $g\in B$ of $\pi$ lies in $H_{D/R}B\subset H_{B/R}$ (Step 4), and the image $\beta(g)=\pi\cdot1_\Lambda$ of $\pi$ in $\Lambda$ lies in $J:=H_{B/R}\Lambda$, the ideal of $\Lambda$ generated by $\beta(H_{B/R})$. Consequently $\pi^8\Lambda\subset J\subset\sqrt J$.

proof.text: (Property (a): $R_\pi\to B_\pi$ is smooth.) Let $g\in B$ be the image of $\pi$, so $B_\pi=B_g$. By Step 5, $g\in H_{B/R}$, so $B_g$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [lem-weil-pbc-singular-ideal-localization-smooth]. By base change [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (1) with $R'=R_\pi$, the ring map $R_\pi\to R_\pi\otimes_RB_g$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] (multiplicative set $M=\{1,\pi,\pi^2,\dots\}$, $\psi:R\to B_g$), the map $B_g\to B_g\otimes_RR_\pi$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, is a localization of $B_g$ at the powers of $g/1$; since $g/1$ is already a unit of $B_g$, this localization map is bijective (injective: $(g/1)^kb=0$ implies $b=0$; surjective: every element is $b\cdot(g/1)^{-k}$ times a unit, i.e. $(b(g/1)^{-k})\otimes1$). Its inverse $\theta:R_\pi\otimes_RB_g\cong B_g\otimes_RR_\pi\to B_g$ is a ring isomorphism with $\theta(x\otimes1)=x\cdot1_{B_g}$ for $x=r/\pi^n\in R_\pi$, because $(r/\pi^n)\otimes1$ and $1\otimes(r/\pi^n)$ both equal $(r\otimes1)(\pi\otimes1)^{-n}$ in the tensor product; so $\theta$ is an isomorphism of $R_\pi$-algebras onto $B_g=B_\pi$ with its $R_\pi$-algebra structure $r/\pi^n\mapsto r g^{-n}$. Smoothness of $R_\pi\to R_\pi\otimes_RB_g$ is therefore smoothness of $R_\pi\to B_\pi$ (the conditions of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] are invariant under isomorphism of $R_\pi$-algebras). This is (a).

proof.text: (Property (b).) Let $\bar\lambda\in\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ be the image of some $h\in H_{\bar C/(R/\pi^8R)}$ and $\lambda\in\Lambda$ any lift of $\bar\lambda$. For every prime $\mathfrak p\supset J$ of $\Lambda$, Step 7 gives $h\in\bar{\mathfrak r}$, i.e. $\bar\lambda\in\mathfrak p/\pi^8\Lambda$, i.e. $\lambda\in\mathfrak p$. Hence $\lambda\in\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in V(J)}\mathfrak p=\sqrt J$ [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], so $\bar\lambda$ lies in the image $\sqrt J/\pi^8\Lambda$ of $\sqrt J=\sqrt{H_{B/R}\Lambda}$ in $\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ (it contains $\pi^8\Lambda$ by Step 5). This image is an ideal of $\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ (the image of an ideal under a surjective ring map), so it contains the ideal generated by all such $\bar\lambda$, i.e. by the image of $H_{\bar C/(R/\pi^8R)}$ under $\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$. This is (b), and with Steps 4 and 6 the lemma is proved.

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 07F0 (smoothing.tex line 1862) and kept. Proof in 8 steps: Stacks applies 07CP and 07CT and omits the verification; written out per delivery-errors D5. Step 1: Ann(pi)=Ann(pi^2) gives Ann(pi^4)=Ann(pi^8) in R and Lambda (induction), so 07CP applies with pi^4 for pi (Stacks leaves this substitution implicit). Step 2: 07CP gives D -> Lambda, rho: C-bar -> D/pi^4 D, D of finite presentation, smooth off V(pi) and at primes over the smooth locus of C-bar. Step 3: the map A/pi^4 A -> D/pi^4 D (A -> A/pi^8 -> C-bar -> D/pi^4 kills pi^4) and its compatibility with Lambda/pi^4. Step 4: 07CT gives B with A -> B -> Lambda, D -> B -> Lambda and H_{D/R}B in H_{B/R}. Step 5: pi in H_{D/R} (non-smooth locus of D inside V(pi), H radical), hence pi in H_{B/R} and pi^8 Lambda in J = H_{B/R}Lambda. Step 6 (a): B_pi smooth over R (singular-ideal localization), base change to R_pi and B_pi (x)_R R_pi = B_pi. Step 7: for a prime p of Lambda containing J, the prime of C-bar under p/pi^8 contains H_{C-bar}, via 07CP (c) and H_{D/R}B in H_{B/R}. Step 8 (b): sqrt(J) as the intersection of primes containing J. No new nodes: every fact used is an existing node of sk-thm-p1 (07CP, 07CT, singular ideal, zero-locus/radical, singular-ideal localization smooth, smooth base change, localization base change). (c), (d) of 07CP and H_{B/D} of 07CT are not needed.
